WRAP around care available at Park Mead – Monday to Friday
It is a pleasure to welcome you to Park Mead. Ours is a school where children are known, valued and encouraged to thrive – both as learners and as people.
At Park Mead, we take pride in being a close-knit, family-friendly community. You’ll find happy, confident children learning alongside staff who are equally enthusiastic about their work. Our curriculum is both adaptive and ambitious, designed to challenge pupils while responding to their individual strengths and interests.
We believe education should be rooted in real experiences, curiosity and care for the world around us. Whether exploring ideas in the classroom, developing teamwork through sport, or discovering nature in our beautiful grounds and Forest School, our pupils are supported to grow into thoughtful, capable global citizens.
Our strong links with families and the wider community are central to school life and alongside our core values – Respect, Resilience, and Responsibility – create an environment where every child feels they belong, achieves their best, and learns to make a positive difference.
I warmly invite you to visit us and see what makes Park Mead such a special place to learn, work and grow.
Heidi WestHead of School

At Pioneer, we feel it is important to prepare pupils for life in a 21st Century world, and it is clear that religion and belief play a central role in local and global affairs. Religious education provides an ideal opportunity to explore matters of religions and non-religious beliefs, to find out what matters most to people in a wide range of traditions, and to discern what is of value for themselves as they develop their own ideas and ways of living.
As of September 2022, we will be following the East Sussex RE Syllabus (2022-27). The syllabus offers teachers the opportunity to plan and to deliver lessons which are informative, engaging and challenging and which will allow pupils to gain a developing understanding of the range of religious and non-religious world views studied, over a period of time. Our two year overview and other resources related to the teaching of RE can be found through further exploration of this page.
KS1/KS2 Curriculum Framework | EYFS Curriculum Framework
Courageous Advocacy – what is a courageous advocate?
A courageous advocate is someone who champions a cause which is special and meaningful to them. At St Mary’s, we teach our pupils that it is important to help others when we can no matter who they are, where they come from or what challenges they may face. We teach this through the teachings of the bible and learning about other courageous advocates. Using our values of Love, Strength and Faith to guide us, we support a range of charities in our local area, nationally and globally. The Pupil Governors work with staff, governors, parents, pupils and St. Mary’s Church to identify worthy causes to support.

We aim to establish a happy and thriving community, both within school and beyond. We encourage our pupils, parents and staff to be generous with their time and think of ways they can show care for our world and people who live in it. Some examples of this include:

pageCache.pageTitle: Key Information About Our Curriculum – The Pioneer Federation
pageCache.text:
Pioneer Vision
Pioneer Vision
‘Being the best that we can be in thriving communities and achieving fullness of life’
We pursue excellence in our classrooms, inclusion in our culture, collaboration across our communities and integrity in all we do – building great Pioneer schools where every child flourishes, every staff member thrives and everyone belongs.
Pioneer Values
Excellence – Inclusion – Collaboration- Integrity
Pioneer Ethos
‘Achievement for All, Learning Together, Learning for Life’
The Pioneer Curriculum
The collaborative Pioneer Curriculum is ambitious, challenging and creative, carefully sequencing knowledge so that children are supported in building a deep understanding across all subject areas. We believe in the importance of providing a high-quality experience that also builds health and well-being individually and collectively. The Pioneer Federation aims to inspire our children to engage confidently with the world and develop the knowledge and skills from across the curriculum that enables them to thrive.
Organisation
Developed collaboratively across the Pioneer Federation, our ambitious, broad and balanced curriculum is carefully sequenced to ensure pupils progressively build, deepen and apply their knowledge and skills over time. Designed specifically for mixed-age classes across Key Stages 1 and 2, our two-year curriculum provides a coherent and systematic pathway that enables all pupils to achieve the National Curriculum expectations and more.
Our Curriculum Overviews set out the strategic intent and sequence of learning across every subject over the two-year cycle. They ensure clear progression and full coverage of the National Curriculum.
Our Subject Overviews explain the intent of each subject, showing how National Curriculum objectives are mapped through carefully sequenced units of learning. They also include our progression of Core and Aspirational Vocabulary, ensuring pupils develop the language needed to become confident learners within each subject.
Our Medium-Term Plans (MTPs) provide the framework for delivering the curriculum each term. They break learning into sequential lesson blocks, identifying the key knowledge, skills, learning activities, expected outcomes and vocabulary for every unit. Each MTP also demonstrates how each school’s unique cultural context is woven into the curriculum. These documents support teachers in planning, adapting and delivering high-quality lessons while ensuring full curriculum coverage.
Our Curriculum & Subject Policies outline the intent, implementation and impact of each curriculum area, demonstrating how our curriculum vision is translated into classroom practice.
Mixed-Age Classes and Curriculum Design
The Pioneer Federation curriculum has been designed specifically for mixed-age classes through a two-year rolling programme. Rather than separating learning by individual year groups, our curriculum provides a shared sequence of progressively-challenging knowledge and skills across each two-year cycle.
Every National Curriculum objective is explicitly mapped within our Medium-Term Plans to ensure that all pupils experience the full curriculum for their year groups over the two years.
Teachers use these documents to deliver lessons with high-quality teaching for all, and adaptations and scaffolds to support children so that the lessons respond to the needs of each cohort. Learning is planned using a ‘stage, not age’ approach, enabling pupils of different ages and abilities to access the curriculum at an appropriate level, while being suitably challenged. This approach ensures every child is supported to make strong progress from their individual starting point.
Adaptation and Inclusion
Our curriculum is designed to be ambitious and accessible for every child.
Teachers adapt planning, teaching and assessment to meet the needs of their individual classes, using the Medium-Term Plans and use ‘Cohort Planning meetings’ to personalise learning for each school and cohort.
At the beginning of every unit, teachers identify pupils’ prior knowledge and build upon it throughout the sequence of learning. This enables teaching to respond directly to pupils’ existing understanding and misconceptions.
Learning is adapted through carefully considered use of language, resources, learning environments, recording methods and assessment approaches, ensuring that every child, regardless of ability, background or starting point, is supported to achieve success and make sustained progress.
Assessment and Monitoring
Assessment is an integral part of teaching and learning and assessments are used to ensure the next steps for learning are clearly defined.
Each unit begins with a Subject Knowledge Organiser, introducing the key vocabulary and essential knowledge pupils will learn. Teachers establish pupils’ prior understanding at the start of each unit before assessing learning throughout the sequence of lessons.
Every unit concludes with a Subject End Point Assessment, enabling teachers to evaluate pupils’ understanding of the key knowledge and skills. These assessments also encourage pupils to reflect on the unit’s overarching enquiry question, promoting deeper thinking and knowledge recall.
Assessment information is used to adapt future planning, address misconceptions and ensure pupils continue to make strong progress. During termly Pioneer Cohort Planning meetings, teachers evaluate the effectiveness of previous Medium-Term Plans before refining subsequent units to meet pupils’ needs.
Subject Leaders from across the Federation regularly monitor the quality of education through subject deep dives, lesson observations, planning reviews and scrutiny of pupils’ work. Senior leaders triangulate this evidence to evaluate teaching, learning and curriculum implementation across the Federation.
Teacher assessments are quality assured through internal moderation, federation-wide cohort moderation, external moderation, pupil tests and regular standardisation training.
Pupil progress is tracked using Pioneer ARBOR tracking and datawalls for all subjects. Termly pupil progress meetings enable teachers and leaders to review attainment, identify pupils requiring additional support and review and plan appropriate interventions.
The Governing Board plays a strategic role in ensuring every school delivers a broad, balanced and ambitious curriculum. Governors monitor curriculum development, pupil outcomes and statutory compliance through regular reports, school visits and analysis of achievement data, providing both support and challenge to school leaders.
Curriculum Sequencing​
The sequence of learning across our curriculum has been carefully planned to maximise progression, engagement and meaningful learning opportunities.
Curriculum sequencing takes account of:
Enrichment
We believe that enrichment is an essential part of a high-quality education. Meaningful experiences beyond the classroom broaden horizons, raise aspirations, deepen learning and contribute significantly to pupils’ personal development.
Through a rich programme of visits, visitors and practical experiences, pupils develop confidence, resilience, teamwork, communication and problem-solving skills while embedding their curriculum learning in meaningful contexts.

Our newsletters, Curriculum Events pages and Forest School updates celebrate these experiences and demonstrate how they enrich pupils’ knowledge, understanding and personal development.

This information is to help pupils and parents or carers understand what our Federation offers and who we work with to support our pupils’ music education.

IMPACT
Children, from their listening, will recognise genres, styles and composers. Children will perform songs and use instruments to an increasingly more complex standard throughout the key stages. Children will have the confidence to improvise and compose using a range of instruments and techniques and will use a range of ways to notate their work.
Teaching and learning
Children will learn to listen carefully and respond physically to a wide range of music. They will play musical instruments and learn a variety of songs from memory, adding accompaniments and creating short improvisation and composition, with increasing confidence, imagination and control. They will explore how sounds and silence can create moods and different effects.

Able, gifted and talented pupils will be supported through the subject, developing analysis, thinking skills and evaluation techniques. The vision of the four Pioneer Federation schools (St Mary the Virgin, Chiddingly Primary, Park Mead and East Hoathly Primary and Nursery) is ‘Achievement for All, Learning Together, Learning for Life’ and this radiates through our policy for children with special educational needs and disabilities.
The Children and Families Act 2014 says that all maintained schools must publish a Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) Information Report every year. This can be found below.
In the report, we explain how we meet our duties towards pupils with special educational needs and disabilities. This report is also the information we provide to the East Sussex local offer which shows the support that is available for children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities in East Sussex: localoffer.eastsussex.gov.uk
The federation schools are mainstream primaries admitting pupils from age 4 -11. East Hoathly also has a Nursery. We are inclusive schools – that means we provide for children with all types of special educational need. Within the Pioneer Federation, it is fully recognised that all class teachers are the teachers of children with Special Educational Needs and disabilities (SEND).
The kinds of SEND that are provided for are categorised into four broad areas of need:
The report below includes details of the processes in place to identify children with SEND and for assessing their needs and required provision.
Emotional Regulation (Zones of Regulation)
Developing children’s emotional development is a really important part of maintaining good mental health and wellbeing. The Pioneer Federation uses the Zones of Regulation programme as a basis for our teaching of strategies to support developing emotional regulation and creating a toolkit of strategies to manage our ever changing emotions. This encourages children to become more self -aware and therefore developing independence and knowledge.
With our younger children we use ‘mood monsters’ to make early links with the colours of the zones system.
Each classroom has display to support emotional regulation. These are adapted according the age and development of each class cohort.
Strategies are taught at various times during the year at a whole class level and revisited on a daily basis. Where needed additional small group or individual work can take place to explore and develop a particular skill or strategy.
More information about the Zones of Regulation can be found here: www.zonesofregulation.com

Background
The Government is providing funding of £150 million per annum to provide new, substantial primary school sport funding. This funding is being jointly provided by the Departments for Education, Health and Culture, Media and Sport, and will see money going directly to primary school Headteachers to spend on improving the quality of sport and PE for all their children.
The purpose of the funding is that schools will have to spend the sport funding in improving their provision of PE and sport, but they will have the freedom to choose how they do this. Allocation Funding for schools will be calculated by the number of primary aged pupils (between the ages of 5 and 11) as at the annual census in January. All schools with 17 or more primary aged pupils will receive a lump sum of £8,000 plus a premium of £5 per pupil. Smaller schools will receive £500 per pupil.
Accountability
Schools will be held to account for how they spend the sport funding. Ofsted has strengthened its coverage of sport and PE within the Inspectors’ Handbook and supporting guidance, so that schools and inspectors know how sport and PE will be assessed in future as part of the school’s overall provision offered.
The Senior Leadership Team at Park Mead Primary School will regularly monitor and assess the impact of the funding and report back to the Governing Body.

East Hoathly Pupil Governors
There are 6 Pupil Governors at East Hoathly, with one child from each year group in KS1 & KS2. They are responsible for helping make decisions about our school, events and fundraising. Each child also holds a secondary role as an RE Council member. They help embed the vision and values within the school community. They consider how the decisions made at school reflect our values.

We meet regularly to share pupil voice, come up with ideas, then feedback to our classes.
St Mary's Pupil Governors
KS1 and KS2 classes have elected one child from each year group to represent their class as Pupil Governor. They are role models for spreading our core values of ‘Love, Strength and Faith’ throughout the school.
Here are some of the ways the pupil governors help the school:
“We help the school become a friendlier environment by taking in people’s ideas and making them feel listened to.”
“We give new ideas in meetings like we fundraise and help charities so we helping to make the world a better place.”
“We help with church and assemblies.”
“It’s nice that we can make big and small changes in the school.”
Park Mead Pupil Governors

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome Message from Our Executive Headteacher – The Pioneer Federation
pageCache.text:
Welcome to the Pioneer Federation of Schools. We are an East Sussex Federation of small primary schools (NOR less than 130 per school).
We have nine schools at present and work as one to achieve the very best for all children and all communities. Through collaboration, we seek to build on the strengths that exist within our schools so that our collective intellectual capital benefits our broader Pioneer community.
We have three collaborative localised clusters (Weald, Downs & Ashdown), each comprising three schools. Clear succession planning is built into Pioneer, with layers of leadership across the Federation. Headteachers and Heads of Schools work within each cluster with development supported by a Lead Cluster Headteacher. The Pioneer Inclusion Lead supports SENCOs and inclusion across the Federation. Pioneer Phase Leaders manage collaborative planning and the curriculum. We also have Pioneer Subject Team Leaders, who manage the development within the collaborative Pioneer curriculum and support cluster subject leadership. Our Pioneer School Business Manager Lead manages the combined budget.
We have a Federated Governing Body, led by our Chair of Governors – Alan Brundle. Each Pioneer Cluster also has a Cluster Committee, led by a Cluster Committee Chair.
We all aim to inspire our children to engage confidently with the world and develop the knowledge and skills from across the curriculum that enables them to thrive. By working as one, we maximise the federated collaborative knowledge and skills of all the adults in our schools. We share the very best practice and are reflective, learning from feedback and from the research that will make a difference to the progress and achievement of all children.
Pioneer Vision
‘Being the best that we can be in thriving communities and achieving fullness of life’
We pursue excellence in our classrooms, inclusion in our culture, collaboration across our communities and integrity in all we do – building great Pioneer schools where every child flourishes, every staff member thrives and everyone belongs.
Pioneer Values
Excellence – Inclusion – Collaboration- Integrity
Pioneer Ethos
‘Achievement for All, Learning Together, Learning for Life’
Pioneer Values Explanation
Excellence
Be the best that we can be – we hold high expectations for every child and every adult.
Inclusion
Achievement for All – every child achieving without exception. We celebrate difference, champion equity and strong adaptations, ensuring no child or team member is ever left behind.
Collaboration
Learning Together – we are stronger together. By sharing knowledge, expertise and trust across our Pioneer schools, we achieve more for every community we serve.
Integrity
Learning for Life – we are honest, transparent and accountable – in every action and every decision.
At Pioneer, we are committed to establishing learning environments that not only stimulate and engage, but also engender a sense of purpose and identity.
Our schools are committed to providing a fully inclusive environment for learning that actively promotes social justice and equity, empowering all to achieve. We create cognitively challenging contexts for learning and build deep and rich knowledge, through adaptive and precise teaching approaches.
The collaborative Pioneer Curriculum is ambitious, challenging and creative, carefully sequencing knowledge so that children are supported in building a deep understanding across all subject areas. We believe in the importance of providing a high-quality experience that also builds health and well-being individually and collectively.
The Federation is a mixture of Community and Church Schools. We value and promote the ethos of each school, ensuring it is firmly at the heart of its community. Our Church Schools work closely with the Diocese of Chichester, under God’s rule and following the example of Jesus. In Matthew 19:26 & John 10:10, Jesus tells us He came to give us life in all its fullness and all things are possible with God, and we believe that we help give children the best start in their education by giving them the values, confidence & stepping stones they need to enjoy all the opportunities life has to offer. We believe that children live their best lives when they know that they are loved and are being loving; shown how to use their strengths so they can continuously work hard and strive for high achievements and are taught that being honest and living their lives by God’s example can lead to ‘life-long learning’ and positive change.
We aim to be the best we can possibly be for every community we serve and to realise the aspirations held for every young person who learns with us.

Across the Pioneer Federation schools we are ‘teaching for mastery in maths’ this phrase describes the elements of classroom practice and school organisation that combine to give pupils the best chances of mastering maths. This approach enables pupils to acquire a deep, long-term, secure and adaptable understanding of the subject.
Intent
Our Mathematics curriculum follows the key aims of the National Curriculum. We aim to ensure that all pupils (regardless of their ability) become fluent in the fundamentals of mathematics and in number so that pupils develop solid conceptual understanding and the ability to recall and apply knowledge rapidly and accurately. Children are taught to reason mathematically by following a line of enquiry, finding connections and establishing relationships whilst using mathematical language. Our mathematics curriculum carefully sequences knowledge, concepts, and procedures to build mathematical knowledge and skills systematically over time.

Organisation
Our exciting, broad and balanced curriculum is taught across our Nursery and Reception Classes. Each term has a focussed topic theme, and key questions for children to consider.
Key Documents
We use key documents to support the ongoing and reflective development of our curriculum, assessment and planning cycles within the EYFS.
Content and Sequence
The EYFS team across the Federation have reviewed the new framework and supporting documents to plan opportunities that deepen children’s understanding, knowledge, skills and language through linking with their local area and community, and enjoying key texts and topic-themed experiences.
Examples of this include:
The curriculum is sequenced in this order to allow pupils to learn and then embed the core foundations they will need to then build upon in each topic and term. For example, the sequence of systematic approach of teaching phonics and number development in Term 1 and 2 will then enable children to access wider activities and provision in subsequent terms, i.e. recognising amounts will support understanding of addition, and grouping or knowing individual phonic sounds will enable children to start early writing through labelling and letter formation.
Vocabulary, language and communication are key areas that thread throughout our curriculum and experiences giving pupils a variety of opportunities to expand and develop their language skills. In addition pupil’s holistic wellbeing will be supported throughout their early years journey, which will include topics such as oral health, mindfulness and self-regulation.
Our specific areas of learning, (Literacy, Maths, Understanding the World and Expressive Art & Design) have all been planned to support children’s learning in line with their open-ended interests and individual schools’ local areas. Some of the others factors also include:
Impact and Knowledge-gained
The skills and knowledge from the different areas of learning are carefully aligned to ensure a correlated cross-curricular approach to the children’s learning, whilst providing flexibility to adapt and follow the individual cohort interests. The curriculum has been designed to allow children regular opportunities to revisit and embed core-learning skills, such as developing vocabulary & language through playing; exploring, reading, writing and mastering early maths concepts. The timetable of the days (weeks, terms and year) is a careful balance of child initiated learning, play and exploration and regular guided teaching moments.
In Early Years the learning is tailored to individual needs and will be made accessible to children through strategies that work for them, this may include sensory activities, calm or quiet zones, through images or signs, brining learning through a specific interest. Children across our early years environments are supported to feel they can express themselves and staff work closely with the SENCO to develop individualised tasks and curriculums for children that are appropriate.
